record.paper_title: Chebyshev Sets, Klee Sets, and Chebyshev Centers with respect to Bregman Distances: Recent Results and Open Problems
record.context_brief: Necessity of supercoercivity for near-Klee single-valuedness
record.original_question: Let X = R^n, let f: X -> [-infinity, +infinity] be a convex Legendre function, let U = int dom f, and define the Bregman distance D(a, b) = f(a) - f(b) - <grad f(b), a - b> for b in U. For a bounded nonempty closed subset C of U, let Q_left,C(y) be the set of points in C maximizing D(., y). Suppose f is twice continuously differentiable and the Hessian grad^2 f(y) is positive definite for every y in U. If f is additionally supercoercive, then Q_left,C is known to be single-valued almost everywhere and generically on U. Is supercoercivity genuinely necessary for this almost-everywhere and generic single-valuedness conclusion?

evidence.quote: Fact 4.4 (See [7, Corollary 5.2.(ii)].) Suppose that f is supercoercive, that f is twice continuously differentiable, that for every y in U, grad^2 f(y) is positive definite, and that C is bounded. Then <-QC is almost everywhere and generically single-valued on U.
Again, it would be interesting to see whether or not supercoercivity is essential in Fact 4.4.
Problem 6. Is the assumption that f be supercoercive in Fact 4.4 really essential?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X=\mathbb{R}^n$ and let $f:X\to[-\infty,+\infty]$ be a convex Legendre function (i.e., a proper closed convex function that is essentially smooth and essentially strictly convex). Set $U=\operatorname{int}\operatorname{dom} f$, and define the Bregman distance
$$D(a,b)=f(a)-f(b)-\langle \nabla f(b),\,a-b\rangle\qquad\text{for } a\in X,\ b\in U.$$
For a nonempty bounded closed subset $C\subseteq U$ and $y\in U$, let
$$Q_{\ell,C}(y)=\Big\{c\in C:\ D(c,y)=\sup_{x\in C}D(x,y)\Big\\}$$
denote the set of left-Bregman farthest points in $C$ from $y$.

Recall that $f$ is called supercoercive if $f(x)/\|x\|\to+\infty$ as $\|x\|\to\infty$.

Assume that $f$ is twice continuously differentiable on $U$ and that the Hessian $\nabla^2 f(y)$ is positive definite for every $y\in U$. It is known that if, in addition, $f$ is supercoercive, then $Q_{\ell,C}$ is single-valued almost everywhere on $U$ and on a generic (i.e., residual) subset of $U$.

Problem: Is the supercoercivity assumption essential for this conclusion? Equivalently, does there exist a convex Legendre function $f$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$ that is twice continuously differentiable on $U$ with $\nabla^2 f$ positive definite throughout $U$, but not supercoercive, together with a bounded nonempty closed set $C\subseteq U$, such that $Q_{\ell,C}$ fails to be single-valued either almost everywhere or generically on $U$?
artifact.status_search_result: A web search surfaces the survey listing this as an open problem and related works on Klee sets and Chebyshev centers for Bregman distances by Bauschke, Macklem, Wang, and collaborators (2009–2010), but no later source was found that resolves whether supercoercivity is essential for the almost-everywhere and generic single-valuedness of the left-Bregman farthest-point map. Status appears unresolved based on available evidence.

status_evidence.title: Chebyshev Sets, Klee Sets, and Chebyshev Centers with respect to Bregman Distances: Recent Results and Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Survey listing open problems about whether supercoercivity is essential for single-valuedness results on Klee sets.
status_evidence.claim: The question is posed as an open problem; no resolution found in subsequent literature.

status_evidence.title: Bregman distances and Klee sets
status_evidence.snippet: Foundational results on Klee sets for Bregman distances assuming supercoercivity.
status_evidence.claim: Prior results assume supercoercivity; necessity is not addressed.

status_evidence.title: Klee sets and Chebyshev centers for the right Bregman distance
status_evidence.snippet: Extends results to the right Bregman distance under supercoercivity hypotheses.
status_evidence.claim: Does not remove or characterize necessity of supercoercivity.
